title: Dominican Republic: Fitch Upgrade to BB, Then a Bigger Deficit | Across the Water, Ep. 20
lede: Fitch upgraded the Dominican Republic from BB- to BB on Nov 3, 2026, citing growth of 4.6% in January–September, an anti-crisis plan and better governance. On Nov 19 the Chamber of Deputies approved a RD$54.1 billion budget increase that lifts the projected 2026 deficit to 4.2% of GDP and suspends the fiscal-responsibility spending rule through Dec 31. This episode explains the upgrade, the growth behind it, the weak spots Fitch flags, and what a stronger peso means for the money Dominicans abroad send home.
keyPoints: Fitch raised the Dominican Republic to BB (stable) from BB- on Nov 3, 2026, level with S&P's BB and Moody's Ba2; investment grade starts two notches higher at BBB- (Fitch via Revista Mercado; Dominican Today).
The economy grew 4.6% in January–September 2026, after 2.1% in 2025; Fitch raised its 2026 forecast to 4.5% from 3.5% (Banco Central RD; Fitch).

The Chamber of Deputies approved a RD$54.1 billion budget amendment on Nov 19: projected deficit RD$365.97 billion (4.2% of GDP), up from RD$280.58 billion; Law 35-24's spending rule suspended through Dec 31; the Senate votes next (Dominican Today).
Interest took 21.9% of government revenue in 2025, almost double the 11.9% median for similar countries (Fitch).

Remittances were US$11.87 billion in 2025 and US$9.49 billion in January–September 2026 (+6.5%); the peso moved from 63.21 to 59.95 per US dollar between Nov 19, 2025 and Nov 19, 2026 (Banco Central RD; DGII).
